scope: The phase-space Brascamp-Lieb datum L_i(d)=(d_i,(Ad)_i), p_i=1/2, is never finite on a real symmetric 3x3 physical block. This refutes using a bare three-coordinate symmetric phase-space BL block as the universal bridge; it does not refute the QFORM conjecture or the finite-BL theorem on larger blocks.
proof_summary: Determinant-one target shears remove the diagonal. For A=[[0,a,b],[a,0,c],[b,c,0]], rank-two kernel generators are k1=(0,-b,a), k2=(c,0,-a), k3=(-c,b,0), with k1+k2+k3=0. If any L_i has rank one, the global BL dimension condition fails. Otherwise V=span{k1,k2,k3} has dimension 1 or 2; in dimension 1 all maps vanish on V, while in dimension 2 each restriction has image dimension at most one, so dim V > (1/2)sum dim L_iV. Hence the BL constant is infinite.
